Micro Cable Merino Wool Hooded Cardigan

Hooded cable knit cardigans are hard to come by, and I swear I’ve had more Sasquatch sightings than sightings of hooded micro cable knit cardigans with flirty “kissing front plackets” that make them even more unique. This Lululemon sweater is definitely a fashion unicorn. Even the linen neps, which give it a stylish, speckled appearance, are random, so no two pieces are identical. While it’s handwash only, it’s a small price to pay for the benefits of warm Merino wool and linen—two natural fibers that are both odor-resistant and antibacterial (so you won’t have to launder it as often as other pieces), extremely breathable, and durable enough to justify the price.

Scuba Oversized Full-zip Hoodie

The fabric of Lululemon's Scuba Oversized Full-zip Hoodie is so soft and smooth, it feels like it should be dry-clean only. (But it thankfully isn’t!) It features an exaggerated oversized fit that is great for layering over other tops, front pockets with a handy interior card sleeve, and thumbholes. Nearly 3,000 shoppers at Lululemon gave it a perfect five-star rating. Their number one complaint is that it doesn’t come in more colors.

Satin Shine High-rise Tight 25"

If I were a fish, I wouldn’t live long because I’m a sucker for anything shiny, including these high-rise tights with a sexy, satin finish. “Felt like Sandy in ‘Grease,’” wrote one shopper who wore them to a holiday party with a peplum blazer and high heels. Other shoppers say these Lululemon leggings are perfect for every activity, ranging from pickleball to jump rope class (how’s that for evidence that they won’t fall down!). They’re ideal for travel because they’re quick-drying and have a back pocket where you can easily hide a credit card or hotel key. The continuous drawcord, meanwhile, ensures they stay put while you’re on your tiptoes, trying to put your bag in the overhead bin or peer over the crowd to catch a glimpse of the Mona Lisa.

Adapted State High-rise Fleece Jogger Full Length

If you’re in the market for a pair of sophisticated sweatpants that you can go the distance in, look no further than these fleece joggers, backed by more than 600 five-star ratings. One shopper wrote, “They started off being my travel pants because they are so comfortable, but now they’re my everyday pants.” The price point is high, but it’s warranted because you’re getting lots of bells and whistles, starting with four-way stretch, a water-repellent finish, zippered cuffs, and zippered pockets. Plus, thanks to the cinchable drawcord in the waist, they’ll stay up, even during an active day.

All Aligned Ribbed Long-sleeve Henley Dress

The only downside of buying this ribbed Henley dress is the fact that you’ll forever be torn between dressing it up and dressing it down. Wear it with white sneakers, a beanie, and a team scarf on game day, or pair it with satin tights, a faux fur vest, and knee-high boots for dinner at a reservations-required restaurant. Made with a blend of 78 percent nylon and 22 percent Lycra elastane, it stays stretchy without losing its shape. The flattering V-seam on the back that draws attention to the narrowest part of the waist even serves up a healthy dose of va va voom.

Scuba Cropped Anorak

We have Greenlandic Inuits to thank for the anorak, an ingenious jacket that effectively traps heat thanks to the half-zip design. Full-length zippers are convenient, but they also allow cold and moisture to seep in. Lululumon’s take on this classic layer features all of the elements of its beloved Scuba Hoodie, including an oversized hood, cinchable hem, and a kangaroo pocket big enough to store your paws and your passport. But unlike the fleece OG, this Scuba Cropped Anorak is made of a water-resistant and light-as-a-feather nylon.

Fast and Free High-rise Tight 25" 5 Pocket

With as many pockets (five to be exact) as a pair of cargo pants, these high-rise tights are perfect for the traveler who wants a streamlined look with plenty of storage. Choose from four different lengths and several colors, including this warm ash grey that goes with almost anything. Like most of Lululemon’s best-selling bottoms, these feature a drawcord waistband. And because they’re made of the brand’s ultra moisture-wicking Nulux, sweat pretty much evaporates on sight. They also add slight compression. According to one five-star review titled “Flattering and dog-hair friendly,” you can count on enjoying “lift and support in all of the right places.”

All Aligned Ribbed Midi Dress

If you can relate to Goldilocks, you’ll love this universally flattering four-way stretch midi dress that fits just right, regardless of your height. I give the backslit a “PG” rating because it’s for added mobility; think subtle, not suggestive. This dress also gets an A+ in versatility. “I’ve worn it with boots and a linen shirt over top, with sandals and a wide-brim hat for a day in the sun, and with runners and a crossbody bag for a long walk,” wrote one shopper who also pairs it with a sweater for plane rides.

SilkAppeal Side-slit Tank Top

Luxurious silk meets lightweight modal fabric in this breathable baselayer you can wear on its own or under a cardigan. One shopper who travels with this top says they even sleep in it. While simple, the side slits create vertical lines that lengthen the legs. They also allow for a greater range of motion. After all, this wardrobe essential was made with yogis and pilates enthusiasts in mind.

Dance Studio Mid-rise Jogger Full Length

When I worked at Lululemon, these jogger pants danced off the shelves faster than we could keep them stocked. Online, they have nearly 5,000 five-star ratings and are available in three lengths and more than a dozen colors. They were initially designed for the dance studio, but between the lightweight fabric, comfortable drawcord waistband, and secure pockets, they’re perfect for sightseeing and long plane rides, too. A few shoppers even mention wearing them on safari. The lighter colors, which you’ll want to wear in the bush, come with a lining so they won’t be see-through.

Taffeta Removable-hood Long Jacket SLNSH Collection

I recently got the Rain Rebel Jacket. However, I’m almost having buyer’s remorse after eyeing this taffeta trench coat from Lululemon’s collaboration with Saul Nash, a London-based designer famous for making elegant pieces easy to move in (he’s a former dancer). The oversized fit is classic while still ideal for layering over sweaters, and there are plenty of pockets, including deep hand pockets with snap closures. There’s also an interior stash pocket for the removable, cinchable hood. “Stylish and practical,” summed up one shopper who said it will be their new travel jacket.

InsulEight Cold-weather Run Shell

Runners and travelers have a lot in common, including the need for ultralightweight layers that can help them cover some serious ground. This packable run shell is both water-repellent and wind-resistant, and it has a hood even cinches in the back, so it stays put. There’s a hidden phone sleeve in one of the zippered hand pockets and strategically mapped insulation in the torso and hood, where your body needs heat the most. Meanwhile, the underarm vents allow for temperature regulation. I recently spent 30 hours in a row flying from Thailand to Japan to Denver to Montana, and there was a huge difference in climate between the four airports I flew through—this jacket would be the key to covering all my bases.

Insulated Ruched Bomber Jacket

Normally, I’m not a bomber jacket person, but Lululemon has made me a fan. The ruching on the back and sleeves of this bomber jacket adds some femininity to the boxy fit, and the cropped cut practically screams, “Pair me with your favorite high-rise pants.” Practicality-wise, it’s made of a water-repellent and windproof nylon filled with premium PrimaLoft insulation, which is designed to stay warm, even if it gets wet. While some shoppers wish it had exterior hand pockets, others appreciate the interior pockets. “Two big zipped inner pockets give you all the carry room you need,” wrote one shopper who loves the “super sleek, post-modern look.”

StretchSeal Waterproof Down-filled Vest

Even though it’s in the We Made Too Much section, this down-filled vest is still a splurge. But that’s because it’s fully waterproof—the sealed seams keep even the most microscopic drops out—and it’s filled with a 600-power sustainably-sourced goose down with exceptional loft and warmth. It’s basically a parka sans sleeves (plus, a hidden phone pouch in one of the zippered hand pockets). While it doesn’t have a hood, this vest is lightweight enough to wear under a hooded shell, especially if you take advantage of the cinchable waist. “Insanely flattering,” reads one five-star review titled, “Worth the money.” Plus, the collar is lined with a thick fleece to keep your neck cozy.

title: 12 On Running Shoe Deals for its End - of - year Sale
content:
It’s a well-known secret that one of the best times to shop is after the holidays and right before the new year, since retailers offer deep discounts on leftover Christmas inventory. And right now, On Running shoes are at some of their lowest prices, including editor-favorite and bestselling styles like the Cloudswift and Cloudmonster.

The Swiss brand, known for its cloud-like sneakers and podded soles, makes shoes that are plush and supportive, and if you don’t already own a pair, now’s your chance to finally grab one. Whether you’re trying to keep stable on cobblestone streets, running through TSA, or training for your next marathon, On Running sneakers can handle it all. Made with cushy foam, shock-absorbing midsoles, and grippy outsoles, these shoes make it easy to move around without losing your footing. Snag deals up to 38 percent off with prices starting at less than $100 during these special after-Christmas sales.

Best On Running Deals

Sellout risk: On Cloud 6 Sneaker, $120 (originally $160)

So easy to move in: On Cloudflyer 4, $142 (originally $160)

Arch support you can’t beat: On Cloudswift Sneakers, $159 (originally $197)

Max cushioning: On Cloudmonster, $136 (originally $170)

Casual sneakers that go with everything: On The Roger Advantage Sneakers, $130 (originally $170)

On Women’s Cloudboom 1 Shoes

The Cloudboom shoe was designed for runners who want to go the distance, whether they’re training for a 5k or a marathon, so it’s durable, lightweight, and comfortable even when worn for hours on end. Its midsole is made with a special foam that propels you forward, making getting to that next step a little easier. Its cushy feel makes it ideal for days you’ll be on your feet a lot, even if you aren’t a runner. At less than $100, the Cloudboom is the best deal on this list.

On Women’s Cloud 6 Sneaker

As easy to throw on as a slip-on sneaker, the Cloud 6 is built with a knotted lacing system that allows you to throw on the shoe in just seconds. It also features a wide opening, so that you’re not wasting minutes struggling to get your foot into the shoe. To keep your feet pain-free, the Cloud 6 is built with On’s zero-gravity foam, which helps distribute your weight while absorbing impact to make each step bouncy and soft. Its minimalist design (compared to other On shoes) makes it versatile for pairing with all of your casual outfits, from denim to leggings.

On Men’s Cloudflyer 4

Some sneakers that are designed to offer a ton of stability are often stiff, but not the Cloudflyer 4. It’s made with a super-soft tongue that makes the shoe flexible and easy to move in—the plushest in On’s lineup. But the shoe doesn’t sacrifice any of its stability. It’s built with an external heel counter to secure the foot in place, and its outsole offers reliable traction. Its comfort and functional design make it the ideal travel shoe.

On Women’s Cloudhorizon Waterproof Hiking Shoes

If you plan on exploring a few new trails soon or simply want sneakers that won’t get ruined in rain or slush, you’ll want to grab a pair of On’s Cloudhorizon Hiking Shoes. The shoe is designed with an upper that keeps water out while still maintaining some breathability. Its sole uses On’s “missiongrip” to provide a ton of traction and stability on wet and dry surfaces. Even better, it’s lightweight, so it won’t hold you back while you’re carrying a bunch of gear.

On Women’s Cloudsurfer 2 Road-running Shoes

An upgrade from the first version of this shoe, the Cloudsurfer 2’s mesh upper was redesigned to offer even more breathability. It’s made without On’s “speedboard,” a special plate found in its other sneakers, and instead relies only on the shoe’s cloud-like cushioning system. So, walking and running in this sneaker feels a lot smoother and softer than in some other On shoes. While it isn’t ideal for long runs, it’s next-level comfy for all-day wear, whether you’re traveling or running errands.

On Men's Cloudswift 3 Running Shoes

Perfect for packing into tight spaces, like a duffel bag, the sock-like upper on this shoe makes it pretty flexible. It also ensures a snug fit for the wearer since it can adapt to different foot shapes. To add to that, the shoe is also designed with a forefoot rocker that makes transitioning into your next step feel effortless, and midsole cushioning that softens landings on hard surfaces. Whether you want to log more miles on a training journey or just need something that’ll keep you quick on your feet, you’ll love the Cloudswift 3’s pillow-like feel.

On Women’s Cloudnova Form 2

The ultra-low silhouette on the Cloudnova Form 2 makes it feel a little less sporty than other On shoes, making it the perfect everyday sneaker. Its flexible build and wide opening makes it easier to step into than its predecessor, so it’s a breeze to throw on, and its mesh upper is semi-transparent, giving the shoe next-level breathability. Despite its thinner upper, the shoe is built with a thick underfoot wall to make it stable and cushy even on hard, uneven terrain. The lifestyle shoe can stave off foot fatigue, so it’s ideal for all-day wear.

On Women's The Roger Advantage Sneakers

There’s something about the tenniscore aesthetic that feels polished and elevated, and these sneakers are no different. While you can definitely wear The Roger Advantage Sneakers on the court, they’re so easily styled that you can really wear them anywhere, and, since they’re so comfortable, your feet will be pain-free. The outsole of the shoe is built with strategically-positioned grooves that allow your feet to bend and flex naturally, while its inner sock-like construction makes your foot feel secure.

On Women's Cloudswift Sneakers

Perfect for roaming city streets, whether you’re walking across cobblestone or pavement, the Cloudswift is made with a shock-absorbing midsole that minimizes impact to your feet from hard surfaces. Shoppers actually say it provides a ton of arch support. “My arches are extreme and they greatly reduce surface impact transfer,” one reviewer says. Its grippy outsole can keep you stable in wet weather, and its breathable mesh can keep your feet from overheating even when you’ve got your thick winter socks on.

On Women’s Cloudmonster

One of On’s cushiest sneakers, the Cloudmonster is extra bouncy, effortlessly rolling you into your next step. Despite its thick cushioning, it’s super lightweight and easy to move in, so you can walk or run quickly with no restraints when needed. If you value sustainability, you’ll also love that the Cloudmonster’s soft upper is made from recycled polyester. Easy to throw on and designed not to hold you back, this shoe makes the perfect everyday sneaker, whether you’re just running errands around home or sightseeing at a new destination.

On Women’s Cloudeclipse

Made with two layers of On’s “loudTec phase” cushioning and a padded tongue, the Cloudeclipse makes you feel like you’re stepping into a cloud. It offers a plush ride with smooth transitions, so the sneaker’s pretty great for everything, including long runs, recreational walking, travel, and everyday tasks. At 36 percent off, it’s currently the lowest price it’s been in 30 days, which adds to its list of benefits you can’t pass up.

On Cloudsurfer Next

If you’re looking for a shoe that can really go the distance, the Cloudsurfer Next can go miles with ease. Its outsole is made with special rubber pads that improve its grip and durability, and its Helion foam delivers a soft, responsive ride. Its woven mesh upper also makes it breathable and super lightweight, so you’ll never feel like they’re weighing you down. Whether you want to head outside to pick up speed or enjoy the high of slow walking, these sneakers can handle both.

title: Netflix removes Stranger Things mistake after fans spot huge error in 1980s scene
content:
Netflix has quietly edited Stranger Things season 5 episode 7 after fans spotted an Under Armour logo on Holly Wheeler's sleeve - despite the show being set in the 1980s

Netflix has discreetly tweaked a Stranger Things season five episode after sharp-eyed viewers caught a glaring error.

With just one episode remaining before the beloved sci-fi series wraps up for good, Stranger Things season five is racing toward its epic conclusion on Netflix.

Amid complaints from some fans about volume two potentially missing scenes, others zeroed in on a conspicuous blunder in the seventh episode, The Bridge. It comes as one episode was crowned the "worst ever" by furious fans - but do you agree?

READ MORE : Stranger Things fans concerned after spotting worrying clue hours before show's finaleREAD MORE : Michael Jackson's harrowing autopsy reveals grim tattoo detail

Following her escape from Vecna's (played by Jamie Campbell-Bower) twisted memories, Holly Wheeler (Nell Fisher) finds herself restrained against one of his sinister Pain Trees.

She fights her way free with punches and kicks, but attentive viewers quickly spotted the Under Armour logo emblazoned on Holly's left arm, reports the Mirror.

The sportswear brand's appearance makes zero sense, considering Under Armour wasn't established until 1996, while the series takes place in the 1980s—an obvious production slip-up.

Netflix has since corrected the scene, digitally erasing the telltale logo so it now appears as a plain black sleeve. Still, that hasn't stopped viewers from flooding social media to call out the gaffe, with one asking: "How did they not notice this?".

Another commented: "Now that's funny. Duffer Bros missed this one bad", while a third drew parallels to Game of Thrones' notorious Starbucks cup mishap, posting: "Close enough, welcome back GoT season eight."

Before it was taken down, someone else called it a "blink and you'll miss it moment" as another fan questioned how this could have been missed in the first place.

They wrote: "For a show backed by $500 million budget and thousands of professionals, it's really hard to understand how something this basic was overlooked and needed a random person to flag it."

Stranger Things' second-to-last episode disclosed that the Upside Down was actually a wormhole, connecting both Earth and The Abyss where Vecna and The Mind Flayer reside.

The group now intends to destroy the Upside Down, now called The Bridge, in order to defeat Vecna once and for all but will they be successful or is this the start of the end for some of them?

title: Stranger Thing Fans Notice Error in Season 5 with Under Armour Clothing
content:
There have been plenty of people worried that Stranger Things’ final season would “do a Game of Thrones” and ruin the series with some bad scripting decisions. While that hasn’t quite happened (although plenty of viewers have been left less than impressed with the new season) the latest run of episodes has managed to emulate one controversial Thrones moment by including something in a shot that should not technically have been around at the time the series is set.

One eagle-eyed viewer spotted a small mistake in what has been an impeccably nostalgic decade of 80s continuity. In the scene where Holly Wheeler breaks free of Vecna’s clutches, her clothing shows that she is wearing an Under Armour shirt, noticeable by the logo on her sleeve. While many people will not have noticed the logo, won’t know the company it stands for, or will simply just assume it is meant to be there, the problem arises from the clothing company not being founded until 1996. With Stranger Things’ final season being set in 1987, this means the shirt could not have been worn by Holly for almost another decade after the series.

This error has drawn comparisons with the infamous Starbucks cup moment in Game of Thrones’ final season, when a cup was left in shot, along with other errors such as a water bottle appearing one scene, and an extra being seen in modern clothing during the Season 8 premiere. While the Stranger Things gaff will not go down in infamy like the GoT Starbucks incident, it once again proves how hard it is to ensure everything is perfect in a show or movie set in a historical setting.

'Stranger Things' Will See Out 2025 With a Huge Finale

Stranger Things has now released seven of its final eight episodes. While the season opened with a strong start to its final run, the second part of the season has not been received quite as favorably, with Episode 7 scoring the lowest rating of any episode of the entire series on IMDb.

Stranger Things will come to its end on New Year’s Day, revealing how the story of Eleven, Mike, the Upside-Down, Vecna and everyone else in Hawkins, Indiana, comes to its conclusion. With Season 5 completely flipping everything that we thought we knew about what the Upside-Down is, and Vecna’s plans, the stage is now set for a cataclysmic finale that will potentially see the deaths of several prominent characters from the series.

Whether the Duffer brothers can manage to stick the landing is something that we will find out in a few days, but the creators of one of Netflix’s most-watched series have always known where the series was headed. As they previously explained:

"Obviously, it's stressful trying to figure out how you want to end the show. Luckily, it was about six or seven years ago that we knew at least what the final scene is. We always knew what the last 40 minutes were going to be."

Stranger Things is streaming now on Netflix, with the final episode debuting at 8 P.M. ET on December 31, 2026.

title: Nike CEO joins Tim Cook in betting his own money that the stock is bottoming
content:
By Tomi Kilgore

Elliott Hill spent $1 million to buy Nike's stock on the open market for the first time, a week after board member and Apple CEO Tim Cook made a similar purchase

Nike's stock surged after CEO Elliott Hill disclosed open-market purchases - a week after Apple CEO and board member Tim Cook did the same.

Shares of Nike surged Wednesday after investors in the struggling athletic-gear giant learned that another top insider was spending a lot of his own money to bet that the worst may be behind the company.

The latest disclosure of an insider purchase, this one by Chief Executive Elliott Hill, comes with the stock (NKE) set to extend its record-long yearly losing streak to four years, as the iconic sneaker company has fallen behind its competition and as consumers have pulled back on discretionary spending.

The stock, which jumped 4.2% to pace the S&P 500 index's SPX Wednesday gainers, has tumbled 61.8% during its yearly losing streak.

The company's turnaround plan, which it has been working on for a while, appears to include a back-to-basics approach. Nike lured longtime company veteran Hill out of retirement to take over as CEO last year.

And while Nike said in its latest earnings report earlier this month that it could take some time for the plan to be completed, open-market purchases of the stock by those in the know send a strong message that better times are ahead. The company's latest quarterly filing also provided reason for more optimism.

In a Form 4 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission last Tuesday, Nike disclosed that Hill spent $1 million on Dec. 29 to buy 16,388 common shares at an average price of $61.10.

The purchase was coded by the SEC as "P," which is defined as "open market or private purchase" of securities, meaning he spent his own available cash to buy the stock.

While Hill has acquired Nike shares before, none of the previous acquisitions, according to available SEC data going back to 2006, were coded as "P," because they included option grants and the exercising of options.

A week earlier, Tim Cook, the CEO of Apple (AAPL) and a 20-year Nike board member, spent about $3 million of his own money to buy Nike shares on the open market.

Read: Tim Cook did something he hasn't done before - buy Nike's stock on the open market

With Wednesday's gain, Nike's stock has now climbed 11.3% since it closed Dec. 22 at the lowest price since May 6.

The company also filed its 10-Q quarterly report late Tuesday, in which it disclosed performance and inventory position by region.

Stifel analyst Peter McGoldrick said "healthy" levels of inventory in North America substantiated his view that the company's turnaround would be led by its U.S. business.

With the revenue foundation now in place, McGoldrick said he believes "the turnaround is an eventuality," although he can't say when it will happen.

Perhaps he doesn't need to. Cook and Hill appear to have already done that.

-Tomi Kilgore

title: Steph Curry rocks Nike Kobe 11 shoes for Warriors vs . Raptors – NBC Bay Area
content:
Steph Curry's sneaker free-agency tour continued Sunday in Toronto.

And the Warriors superstar's choice of footwear for Sunday's game against the Raptors was extra intentional and sentimental.

During pregame warmups, Curry rocked the "Northern Lights" Nike Kobe 11, the shoes that late NBA legend Kobe Bryant wore during his final All-Star Game in 2016 in Toronto.

He kept the sneakers on throughout the game, too.

It isn't the first time Curry paid homage to Bryant.

Golden State Warriors

In fact, during his first day of sneaker free agency after parting ways with Under Armour, Curry wore Mambacita Kobe 6 Nike shoes while warming up before the Warriors' game against the San Antonio Spurs on Nov. 14.

After that game, Curry explained his decision.

"I know it's weird seeing me in anything else other than my own shoes, but just the idea of what he meant -- I've talked about Kobe a lot. That specific pair, I think it speaks for itself, what it means," Curry told reporters after the win. "Other than that, just something I wanted to take advantage of that moment and pay tribute. I think it gave me some good energy tonight."

Earlier Sunday, Curry arrived to Scotiabank Arena wearing rapper Drake's Nike NOCTA Glide.

It's clear Curry is having fun with his free agency.

title: Pacer Advisors Inc. Sells 59,726 Shares of Columbia Sportswear Company $COLM
content:

title: Nike Quietly Dumps NFT Unit RTFKT as Converse Revenue Drops 30 %
content:
Nike has quietly sold its digital products subsidiary RTFKT, the NFT unit it acquired during the 2021 crypto boom, as the sportswear giant’s Converse brand reported a 30% drop in quarterly sales last December.

The sale, effective December 16, marks Nike’s definitive exit from blockchain-based collectibles and signals a strategic retreat to its core athletic performance business under the new leadership of CEO Elliott Hill.

The sportswear giant had previously announced plans last year to end its non-fungible token (NFT) operations and other blockchain-based initiatives.

Nike Dumps NFT and Metaverse Ambitions

RTFKT was acquired by Nike in 2021 under then-CEO John Donahoe, who prioritized direct and digital sales channels during his tenure, betting heavily on emerging technologies and virtual consumer experiences.

The acquisition was designed to expand Nike’s presence in collectibles and metaverse markets during the 2020-2021 NFT and digital worlds bubble, when virtual sneakers and avatars commanded premium prices from collectors and crypto enthusiasts.

In a brief statement, Nike said the RTFKT sale was “launching a new chapter for the company and its community,” adding that it “continues to invest in delivering innovative products and experiences across physical, digital and virtual environments.”

The carefully worded announcement left room for continued digital initiatives while distancing the company from its blockchain experiments.

Terms of the RTFKT sale, including the buyer’s identity and financial details, were not disclosed.

When asked who purchased the unit, Jarlan Perez, Yuga Labs Design Director and former Nike and Google executive, responded cryptically:

“That’s up to them to reveal themselves whenever they are ready,” suggesting the buyer may be a prominent player in the digital assets space.

Despite the uncertain future, RTFKT tokens surged by over 270% following reports of the sale, sparking speculation that new ownership could revive the “lost glory” of NFTs.

Legal Troubles Shadow NFT Exit

Nike faces mounting legal pressure over its abrupt departure from digital collectibles, complicating what was already a challenging strategic pivot.

Some purchasers of Nike-themed NFTs and other crypto assets filed a proposed class action lawsuit in Brooklyn federal court last April, seeking damages of at least $5 million for what they characterize as an abandonment of promised digital ecosystems.

Lead plaintiff Jagdeep Cheema, an Australian investor, claims that Nike’s abrupt decision to shut down RTFKT wiped out the NFTs’ value without adequate notice or compensation.

title: New Balance 1080v15 review | Tom Guide
content:
The New Balance 1080 line of running shoes has been a go-to option for people seeking a comfortable daily trainer in recent years, and I’ve rated the past couple of models of the 1080 as great options for new runners in particular.

Brands tend to play it safe with their most popular shoes and only make incremental updates to them, but the New Balance 1080v15 is a big change from the New Balance 1080v14 thanks to a brand-new midsole foam called Infinion.

The New Balance 1080v15 is a lighter and more impressive daily trainer than its predecessor thanks to this new midsole, but some of the best running shoes available come in a little cheaper. My colleague Jessica Downey and I have been racking up the miles in the shoe over the past few weeks. Here’s our full New Balance 1080v15 review.

New Balance 1080v15 review: Price & availability

The New Balance 1080v15 will launch globally on 15 January 2026. It costs $170 / £170, which is a small price rise on the 1080v14, which cost $165 / £160 at launch and can now be found in sales fairly regularly.

While premium cushioned running shoes have become very expensive in recent years, this price still makes the New Balance 1080v15 one of the pricier daily trainers we've tested in 2025.

New Balance 1080v15 review: Design & fit

I tested the white color of the New Balance 1080v15 for our review, while Jess was lucky enough to try the bright lime green shoe, which is certainly distinctive. We’d suggest sticking to your normal running shoe size with the 1080v15.

The 1080v15 has dropped in weight compared to the 1080v14, with the new shoe weighing 9.2oz in my US men’s size 9.5, compared to 10.1oz in the same size for the 1080v14. I’ve tried the last five models of the 1080, and this is the lightest one yet.

It has a stack height of 40mm at the heel and 34mm at the forefoot for a 6mm drop, which gives you a little more foam underfoot than with the 1080v14. It’s not as maxed out on this front as many running shoes these days, but the New Balance 1080v15 is certainly still cushioned and comfortable.

Upper

The 1080v15 has a new contoured mesh upper with raised sections on it. The material felt a little stiff at first, but once I slipped my feet in, it was comfortable, and I didn’t notice the upper at all in my runs, which is always a good sign.

For a cushioned shoe, it’s not overly padded around the tongue and collar either, and I’d say it’s more breathable than many sneakers in its category.

Midsole

The main update to the 1080v15 is its new Infinion midsole, which replaces the Fresh Foam X foam used on the past few models of the shoe.

This is a lighter, more responsive material than Fresh Foam X, and gives the shoe a livelier feel than its predecessor while still retaining the comfort you expect from the 1080 line.

Outsole

Along with the new foam, another reason why the 1080v15 is light for a cushioned shoe is that it doesn’t have the most extensive outsole.

There is rubber covering the heel and forefoot of the shoe, but there’s a lot of exposed foam in the midfoot area. This shouldn’t be a major problem with regard to durability, since the main areas of wear and tear on a shoe are the heel and forefoot, but the 1080v15 might not be as hard-wearing as a shoe with a fuller rubber outsole.

New Balance 1080v15 review: Running performance

NHF: The New Balance 1080v15 is a daily trainer that’s built primarily to offer comfort on easy runs, but the lighter design of the shoe also means that it is a capable option at faster paces as well.

During my testing, I used it for a long run, several easy runs, and a couple of easy-to-steady progression runs, and it is a more versatile running shoe than many highly-cushioned options, thanks to its lighter, more agile design.

The new Infinion foam in the midsole is well-balanced, in that it’s neither excessively soft and mushy nor too firm. It does deliver comfort and protection, but has a bit of pop off the toes as well.

It’s not quite as lively as some other foams I’ve tested in cushioned shoes, though, such as the springy ZoomX used in the Nike Vomero Plus, or the responsive Nitro Foam used in the Puma Velocity Nitro 4. As a result, I didn’t find the New Balance 1080v15 as good for speed sessions or tempo runs as it was for easy efforts.

My other concern with the foam is that it felt like it compressed during the course of my longest run in the shoe, which was around 13 miles, and most notably in the forefoot, it lost some of its bounce during the run.

JD: I used the 1080v15 for a mix of training runs, including easy miles, faster intervals, fartlek sessions, and one longer run with mixed pacing. At first glance, the shoe looked a little cheap and flimsier than I expected, and the mix of neon and metallic silver didn’t help.

Honestly, it definitely did not look like a $170 shoe to me. But once I stepped in and walked around, my opinion changed. The shoe is very comfortable right out of the box.

The upper is soft, stretchy and really well ventilated. Underfoot, the foam is very soft and cushy. Although I was happy with just how comfortable they felt at first, I could feel my heels sink slightly when walking, which made me wonder how it would feel running. However, on the run, I didn’t find myself feeling like I was fighting to rebound or to keep up a strong momentum.

The 1080v15 feels noticeably lighter than the 1080v14, and the new Infinion midsole gives it a much more energetic and fun feel. The rocker geometry looks subtle, but the heel-to-toe transition felt smooth and natural to me. I especially enjoyed the light, responsive feel when hitting any incline.

Overall, I think this is a really solid daily trainer. If I had to choose between keeping the 1080v14 or the 1080v15, I would go with the 15. It feels lively, versatile and makes a range of runs feel easier. I could quite easily wear it for all my training runs, provided I wasn’t fussed about having a shoe rotation or dealing with the eye-watering neon colorway I tested.

Should you buy the New Balance 1080v15?

Nick Harris-fry The New Balance 1080v15 is a very capable running shoe that works well for daily training, offering a lot of comfort in a fairly lightweight design. It’s a good update on the previous model in my opinion, bringing the weight of the shoe down while retaining its high level of cushioning.

Compared to the market at large, however, there are some strong options available at around the same price, or less. The Nike Vomero Plus is a softer, bouncier shoe that I prefer for all kinds of runs, while the Asics Novablast 5 and Hoka Clifton 10 are very capable shoes with more rockered rides that come in cheaper than the New Balance 1080v15.

I’m also a big fan of the Puma Velocity Nitro 4, which is lighter and more affordable than the New Balance 1080v15, and has a more energetic foam in its midsole. The Puma shoe is narrower and not quite so cushioned as the New Balance, but I still found it comfortable for long runs myself.

If you pick up the New Balance 1080v15, then I doubt you’ll be disappointed by it, but in a crowded market, it doesn’t do enough to stand out for me, and the Infinion foam lacks some of the dynamism you can find elsewhere.

Jessica Downey: If you’ve had your eye on the New Balance 1080 line, the 1080v15 is definitely a strong premium daily trainer. It feels light, energetic, and for me, a step up from the 1080v14 in terms of responsiveness. That said, aesthetics are subjective. The bold colorway and silver detailing will not appeal to everyone, and it sits at the higher end of the daily-trainer price range.

If the 1080v15’s price is a concern, there are more affordable daily trainers worth considering. Within New Balance, the Rebel v5 offers a lighter, versatile daily trainer at a lower price point. If you’re open to other brands, the Asics Novablast 5 delivers a lively, cushioned ride that works well for mixed-pace training while also being easier on the wallet.

title: Paul Mescal Endorses Adidas Sambas at a Screening for  Hamnet
content:
Few sneakers have had a run quite like Adidas Sambas. First introduced in 1949 and adopted by soccer players, the kicks were crowned the Shoe of the Year at the 37th annual FN Achievement Awards in 2023. And while the silhouette may ebb and flow in popularity, Paul Mescal is proving the look still has legs in 2026.

On Friday, the actor attended a screening for his latest film, “Hamnet,” at The London West Hollywood, clad in a pair of black Adidas Sambas. Typically retailing for $100, the fan-favorite shoes are defined by a low-profile silhouette, as well as a grain leather upper with suede and gold foil details. Meanwhile, the shoes are also recognized by their signature gum sole, which is naturally tackier than standard rubber and can grip better on slick flooring. Though Mescal opted for the classic — and perhaps most sought-after — black style (which he’s worn on numerous occasions in the past), the Sambas come in a medley of colors, from emerald green to dusty pink.

The “Normal People” star wore the famous sneakers with a laid-back look consisting of a black long-sleeve polo shirt over a white tee, finished with relaxed light-wash jeans. As part of the event, Mescal, who portrays William Shakespeare in the film (which was adapted from Maggie O’Farrell’s 2020 novel), chatted with Antonia Blyth, a British writer based in Los Angeles. “Hamnet” also stars Jessie Buckley, Joe Alwyn and Noah Jupe.

title: Lululemon Founder Chip Wilson Launches Proxy Fight to Change Board
content:
Lululemon Athletica founder Chip Wilson is launching a proxy fight at the athletic-apparel retailer in an effort to remake the company’s board while Lululemon searches for a new chief executive.

Wilson said Monday that he has nominated three director candidates to the company’s board, confirming an earlier report by The Wall Street Journal.

The nominees are former On Running co-CEO Marc Maurer, former ESPN Chief Marketing Officer Laura Gentile and former Activision CEO Eric Hirshberg.

Wilson isn’t trying to put himself back on the board, which might come as a surprise to some given his recent efforts to publicly target the company he started. He remains Lululemon’s second-biggest shareholder, with a nearly 9% stake, according to FactSet. (Vanguard is the largest holder.)

“I know this campaign for change cannot be about me,” Wilson said. “It is about recommitting Lululemon to genuine creative leadership that will re-establish a brand of enduring strength.”

Activist investors often tap former company executives to help them shake up targets, but it is rare to see a founder of a company turning to a hostile approach such as a board fight.

Lululemon is in the midst of an identity crisis and earlier this month said that its CEO, Calvin McDonald, will step down in January. Its stock is down 45% this year, while the broader market has rallied.

Pressure had been mounting for McDonald to turn around the business, including from Wilson, who had been publicly criticizing him and the company for killing innovation and “losing its cool.” Sales have recently stagnated in the U.S., with newer rivals such as Alo Yoga and Vuori eating at market share.

The Journal previously reported that Wilson had tapped financial advisers and was considering waging a proxy battle before Lululemon’s nomination window closes at the end of this month.

Maurer, who stepped down as On Running co-CEO at the end of June, helped build a leading sportswear brand. Gentile founded ESPNW, ESPN’s brand dedicated to women. And Hirshberg oversaw top franchises including “Call of Duty” during his time at Activision, the largest segment of Activision Blizzard.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook Just Gave Nike Investors 3 Million Reasons to Cheer
content:
It's been tough sledding for the iconic sports apparel company Nike (NKE +1.55%), which has seen its stock shed roughly 19% this year and over 57% in the past five years. Retail brands like Nike have been challenged by rising competition in the space, more price-sensitive consumers, and macro challenges, among others.

Nike has also acknowledged strategic mistakes, including an overemphasis on online promotions and a lack of product innovation. Recently, however, Apple's CEO Tim Cook, who has been on Nike's board of directors for about two decades, gave Nike investors 3 million reasons to cheer.

Tim Cook doubles down on Nike

Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings recently revealed that Cook purchased 50,000 shares of Nike at an average price of $58.97 per share, totaling nearly $3 million. Cook made the purchases on the open market, and the move nearly doubles his stake in the company. According to MarketWatch, these purchases are also Cook's first market buys since 2005, not including equity-based compensation or purchases associated with derivatives.

Insider buys indicate bullishness, and shares jumped after the SEC filings were made public. As the CEO of Apple, Cook possesses keen business acumen and carries more recognition than the typical board member, so it makes sense that his purchases are being received positively. They also come as Nike is attempting a large turnaround plan that has struggled to gain momentum thus far.

Nike recently reported earnings results for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026. The actual earnings results came in strong when the company reported $0.53 earnings per share on revenue of $12.4 billion, both of which came in ahead of Wall Street estimates. However, the stock got crushed after management delivered disappointing guidance, especially as it pertains to its business in China, which is viewed as a key market for the company.

Can Nike figure it out?

Nike's turnaround plans involve an intense refocus on athletes, the brand, and product innovation. Under Hill, the company has seen positive traction regarding its new product lines, which is reflected in improved revenue for the North American business. However, the company is also dealing with headwinds outside of its control, due to tariffs.

China is likely the biggest challenge for Nike right now. The company needs to determine how to better connect with consumers in terms of its brand and products, as well as how to most efficiently reach them in China. Nike is making changes in the region, but investors will likely need to see more proof that the strategy is working.

title: Stranger Thing Fans Call Out Under Armour Error In Season 5
content:
In a show as big and sprawling as Stranger Things, there are bound to be a few slip-ups. Ever since the sci-fi series premiered in Season 1, it’s been consistently called out for plot holes in its complicated story, but the latest inaccuracy that’s gone viral all comes down to one misplaced logo.

In the penultimate episode of the series, Holly Wheeler is able to free herself from Henry Creel’s mind prison, waking up to find she’s actually been engulfed in a fleshy cocoon on Vecna’s home world, the Abyss. As she sticks her arms and legs out of the membrane, viewers noticed an Under Armour logo blatantly displayed on one of Holly’s sleeves.

This is an anachronistic error, since Under Armour was not founded until 1996, but Season 5 of Stranger Things is set in 1987. Sure, Holly is on an alien planet in this scene, but you’d think her clothes wouldn’t magically transform into future athleisure-wear for no reason. As the wardrobe error went viral on social media, fans began comparing the mistake to “the Starbucks cup in Game of Thrones Season 8.” In case you forgot, the final season of Game of Thrones faced similar anachronistic backlash when fans pointed out an errant Starbucks cup during a feast scene.

It should be noted that since the mistake was pointed out shortly after Season 5, Episode 7 dropped on Dec. 25, Netflix has seemingly edited the Under Armour logo out of the scene. As of Dec. 29, Holly’s sleeve no longer seems to sport the anachronistic brand.

This wardrobe slip-up may be small, but it’s one of several issues fans have had with Stranger Things’ final season. Since its premiere on Nov. 26, Season 5 has been called out for confusing relationship scenes, strangely worded speeches, and unexplained character absences. The backlash has led to an overwhelming amount of negative fan reviews on sites like Rotten Tomatoes and IMDb, making this is show’s worst-rated season.

At least the Under Armour problem was easy for Netflix to fix. The other stuff probably won’t be a simple edit.

title: March trial scheduled in long - running Nike sex discrimination lawsuit
content:
A federal judge on Thursday ruled against a last-minute effort to convert a long-running sex discrimination lawsuit against Nike into a class action.

She also ordered a five-day trial, starting March 2, on the claims of the only remaining plaintiff.

The lawsuit, filed in August 2018, described Nike as a place where “women are devalued and demeaned” and systematically underpaid or passed over for promotions, allegations the company has consistently disputed.

In Thursday’s four-page ruling, U.S. District Judge Amy Baggio cited the “unreasonable delay” of the request to make a second argument for certifying a class, which, if successful, could have extended any ruling or monetary award to a broader group of alleged victims. She noted the motion happened “a full year” after plaintiffs discovered new evidence they wanted to present to the court.

Nike and attorneys for plaintiffs didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

The ruling means the lawsuit, which was filed seven-and-a-half years ago, is finally on the verge of resolution, at least at the trial court level.

“This is the end of the line,” said University of Washington law professor Jeff Feldman, who added any appeals likely won’t be heard until after the March trial, which is less than seven weeks away.

“This case is going to be over in March, one way or another,” he said.

The two sides reached a tentative settlement nearly a year ago, less than a month before a previously scheduled trial. Since then, they’ve resolved the claims of all plaintiffs, except for one.

But they’ve been unable to finalize the terms of a tentative class settlement, which would have included additional women who worked at Nike in recent years.

In August, the two sides asked Baggio to step in and help resolve the matter.

At a roughly 45-minute hearing in September, a lawyer for Nike said the tentative class settlement would have paid a “significant amount of money” to members, but she said plaintiffs scuttled it by changing a key term after reaching a deal.

The lawyer did not provide details of the tentative settlement, but she said it fell apart because plaintiffs’ lawyers wanted to limit how much legal insulation Nike would have from similar claims.

At the hearing, a lawyer for plaintiffs said a deal had not been reached and asked the court to reconsider the 2022 decision not to convert the lawsuit into a class action, citing “changes to the evidentiary record,” namely a set of unofficial workplace complaints called the Starfish survey that Nike partially withheld in response to initial discovery orders.

At the September hearing, Baggio said the case had been “lingering way too long in the court.”

She expressed similar impatience in Thursday’s ruling, noting plaintiffs had new evidence “a full year prior” to asking for permission to file a second motion for class certification.

It’s unclear if plaintiffs can still try to finalize or enforce the tentative class settlement reached last year.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook Just Loaded Up on Nike Stock . Should You ?
content:
Key Points

Tim Cook bought 50,000 shares of Nike stock.

The Apple CEO is a director on Nike's board.

Nike recently returned to top-line growth, but there are still some major concerns.

10 stocks we like better than Nike ›

When Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) CEO Tim Cook purchased 50,000 shares of Nike (NYSE: NKE) in late December, it got a lot of attention and even sent shares of the athletic apparel and shoe company sharply higher. After all, not only is Cook a successful businessman, but he is a Nike insider. The CEO sits on Nike's board of directors.

Investors sometimes treat insider buying as a simple signal: management (or board members) think the stock is undervalued. Sometimes that's right. But investors shouldn't follow blindly.

So, is Nike stock a good buy today or not? Let's take a look.

Cook's buy matters, but so does the context

Notably, Cook's purchase was an open market one. This means it wasn't part of a stock option compensation plan (or a similar plan). Rather, he had to pay full price for his shares. Additionally, the purchase was sizable, totaling nearly $3 million. It also nearly doubled his stake in the company. Given the size of the purchase and the significant increase in Cook's stake, it's not surprising that the market interpreted the purchase as good news.

Still, it's important to remember that Cook is a Nike director.

That doesn't mean the purchase is meaningless. But it does mean he may have incentives beyond pure return maximization. Directors often want to demonstrate alignment with shareholders, reinforce confidence during a rough stretch, or meet (or stay ahead of) internal ownership expectations. In other words, it can be both a sincere vote of confidence and a governance-minded move.

A rough patch

Investors should look beyond Cook's purchase to answer this simple question: Does Nike's business momentum (or lack of it) and valuation offer an attractive risk-reward right now?

Unfortunately, I don't think so.

Nike's turnaround is making progress, but the business still looks challenged.

Revenue in the company's second quarter of fiscal 2026 (a period ended on Nov. 30, 2025), rose just 1% year over year. Further, the composition of this revenue was probably even more discouraging than this anemic headline figure. Yes, wholesale revenue rose 8% year over year, but its higher-margin Nike Direct revenue fell 8%. Nike Direct is the company's direct-to-consumer channel, made up of Nike-owned stores and sales through its digital platforms. So, this channel speaks to the company's brand power with consumers, given how directly these channels are tied to its business and to consumers.

Nike's profitability also moved in the wrong direction. Gross margin fell 300 basis points to 40.6%, and net income declined 32% to $792 million.

Some of Nike's near-term problems are self-inflicted as it tries to reposition parts of its business and sharpen its product and brand message so that it can perform better over the long term. But Nike still has a lot of work to do.

"NIKE is in the middle innings of our comeback," said Nike CEO Elliott Hill in the company's latest earnings release, adding that the company is working through its "Win Now" strategic actions, including "strengthening partner relationships" and "rebalancing our portfolio..."

Meanwhile, the athleisure space remains intensely competitive, as the company faces major competition from younger brands like Lululemon, Vuori, and Hoka, as well as more established brands like Adidas. Of course, Nike's brand still has enormous global equity. But consumers have more choices than ever.

A look at valuation

I'd be more willing to recommend Nike in the middle of its turnaround and an intensely competitive environment, but shares arguably don't look cheap enough. Sure, the company's dividend yield of 2.6% is solid, and Nike has an exceptional balance sheet. But with earnings moving in the wrong direction and sales barely growing, it's tough to justify the stock's price-to-earnings ratio of 37.

Even Nike's forward price-to-earnings is high, at 40. Measuring its price as a multiple of analysts' expected earnings per share over the next year, the fact that Nike's forward price-to-earnings ratio is higher than its trailing price-to-earnings ratio shows that analysts expect earnings to remain under pressure.

Given the competitive intensity in athleisure, declining sales in its direct-to-consumer channel, margin pressure, and ongoing uncertainty as far as tariffs go, I personally will be staying on the sidelines.

Cook's buy in Nike stock is interesting. But, for me, that's about all it is.

title: Lululemon founder launches a proxy fight to reshape apparel maker board
content:
Lululemon Athletica's founder Chip Wilson said on Monday he had launched a proxy fight by nominating three independent directors to the company's board, days after the Canadian apparel maker announced the exit of CEO Calvin McDonald.

Lululemon has struggled to find its footing with younger and affluent shoppers amid stiff competition from fast-growing newer rivals like Alo Yoga and Vuori, as well as pressure from activist investor Elliott Management.

Wilson has nominated three director candidates to Lululemon's board, including former On Running co-CEO Marc Maurer, former ESPN chief marketing officer Laura Gentile and former Activision CEO Eric Hirshberg.

"The recent CEO change announcement was the third total failure of board oversight with no clear succession plan in place. Shareholders have no faith that this board can select and support the next CEO without input from a board with stronger product experience," Wilson said in a statement.

Earlier this month, the company said McDonald would step down in January, joining a long list of leadership shake-ups across global consumer companies and retailers.

Lululemon did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The Wall Street Journal first reported the news.

title: Stranger Things fixes editing mistake after fans called out anachronistic piece of clothing
content:
The editors of Stranger Things have quietly fixed an error after fans noticed a historically inaccurate piece of clothing in the new season five episodes.

After the latest volume of the Netflix series was released December 25, viewers quickly pointed out that Holly Wheeler, played by Nell Fisher, was wearing an Under Armour shirt while she was trapped in Vecna’s lair in episode seven.

Under Armour was not founded until 1996 — nine years after the episode was set in 1987.

It took just a week of fans’ complaints about the anachronistic item for the series’ co-creators to edit the popular sportswear logo out of the new episodes ahead of the volume three release scheduled for New Year’s Eve. Netflix did not immediately return The Independent’s request for comment.

“Stranger things trying to ‘Mandela effect’ us. They really went and edited out the UnderArmour logo on Holly’s shirt,” one fan reacted on X. Another added, “Just rewatching the last episode before the finale of Stranger Things, looks like they’ve fixed Holly’s under armour sleeve.”

Before the branding was cut from the scene, viewers took to social media to joke about the accident, with one writing on X: “Didn’t know under armour was in the upside down.”

“Holly wearing Under Armour in season five of [Stranger Things] is more unsettling than Vecna,” another joked. “Did she tear through the fabric of space and time and go into the future?! I’m mostly joking but need clarity.”

The editing snafu is reminiscent of other times that popular TV shows forgot to edit out an anachronistic item.

Back in 2019, the internet was set ablaze when a Starbucks coffee cup was spotted in the background of a season eight episode of Game of Thrones. The item was completely out of place among the goblets and animal horns in the HBO fantasy series, and the production gaffe forced showrunners to issue a statement at the time acknowledging their mistake. The show’s errors continued when a water bottle was later seen in the series finale, prompting some fans to even call for a remake of the last season.

The Under Armour mistake was not the only reason that Stranger Things fans complained about the new season five episodes. The newest season of the hit science fiction show has sparked criticism among viewers, as many people have been disappointed by the latest installments. Many viewers had hoped for more action and at least one surprising death, but have instead found the storylines to be lackluster.

The fifth and final season’s penultimate volume was released on Christmas Day, nearly 10 years after the show premiered in 2016.

The Stranger Things finale will be released on Netflix on Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET.

title: Nike’s Foamposite Sneaker Is Getting an Unexpected ‘Stranger Things’ Collaboration
content:
Netflix’s “Stranger Things” may be over, but Nike, Inc. still has more officially licensed sneaker collaborations to come with the hit franchise.

After a new unreleased batch of x Converse sneakers recently surfaced, yet another collaboration has appeared, and it may be the most unexpected pair yet. Official e-commerce product images show a new Stranger Things x Nike Air Foamposite One PRM QS in detail.

With a Black/Bright Crimson/Off Noir colorway, the upcoming release gets a red lightning-covered graphic across its black upper. A leather eyestay is accented with metallic mini Swooshes near the toe and, in a nod to the show’s Upside Down dimension, a flipped Penny Hardaway “One Cent” logo on the heel. The shoe also includes shaggy, Vecna-like shoelaces and printed pull tabs which feature the character’s “found you” line on the inside. The villain is also referenced on the shoe’s graphic insole.

While the Air Foamposite One model, which originally released in 1997, isn’t necessarily period-accurate for the 1980s setting of the show, the discrepancy likely won’t keep fans from trying to get their hands on this .

Nike’s Stranger Things collaboration began in 2019 and has featured models including the Air Max 1, Blazer, Converse Chuck 70, Cortez, Dunk Low, Field General High, LD-1000 and Tailwind 79.

Beyond the special-edition Stranger Things style, fans can expect more Air Foamposite Ones in February including NBA All-Star Weekend iterations. However, the Swoosh-adorned version of the shoe, the Air Foamposite Pro, is set to have an even busier year with numerous reissues and new styles on the way.

The Stranger Things x PRM QS is expected to be released Feb. 13 with a retail price of $250. Given its Quickstrike titling, fans can count on limited-edition availability for the collaboration. The sneaker has a style code of IR7336-001 and will be available from Nike’s Snkrs app and select Nike Sportswear retailers.

title: Nike CEO buys $1 million in stock, shares inch higher to close the year
content:
Nike CEO Elliott Hill this week purchased roughly $1 million in stock, the latest sign of his confidence in an ongoing turnaround effort.

Hill was the third Nike insider to buy stock in the past two weeks.

Apple CEO Tim Cook, a longtime Nike board member, nearly doubled his stake in the company on Dec. 22, purchasing roughly $3 million in shares. Former Intel CEO Bob Swan, also a Nike board member, purchased $500,000 in shares on Dec. 22.

The flurry of insider purchases gave Nike’s stock a boost at the end of a lackluster trading year.

Shares climbed 4% Wednesday, but they were down 16% for the year. That’s well below the overall market. The S&P 500 – an index of 500 large company stocks – rose 16% this year.

But as Hill’s second year as chief executive gets underway, and as evidenced by the stock purchase, he remains optimistic that his comeback plan for Oregon’s biggest company is working.

Since taking the helm in October 2024, Hill has worked to reboot Nike’s culture, including naming the company’s campus after co-founder Phil Knight.

After leaning too hard on retro sneakers and direct sales, he refocused the company on sports and rebuilt relationships with wholesalers.

Hill has also accelerated efforts to develop new products and show that Nike’s innovation muscles haven’t shriveled. In October, Nike unveiled several daring new products including a jacket that inflates and a pair of motorized walking shoes.

To close the year, Hill made a few changes to Nike’s executive ranks designed to further speed up corporate decisions.

Two weeks ago, the company reported mixed earnings that included a second consecutive quarter of slightly increased sales after five quarters of declines.

But Nike’s stock plunged 10% in the immediate wake of the report because of a lackluster sales forecast and a bruising performance in China, where revenue decreased 17%. Tariffs also remain a significant headwind for Nike, amounting to $1.5 billion in new annual costs.

Some stock analysts have grown impatient with a corporate rebound effort that’s about to enter its third calendar year.

“The Nike turnaround is still struggling to gain traction and continues to take longer,” Tom Nikic, an analyst at the research firm Needham, wrote in a note to investors this month. “While we agree with management’s overarching strategy … it’s becoming evident that the company’s issues prior to … Hill’s arrival were far deeper than we initially realized.”

On a conference call with analysts after the earnings report, Hill pointed to the company’s performance in North America as proof that the new strategy is working.

“As our largest business, that’s where much of our focus has been,” Hill said.

In the quarter, Nike’s sales in North America increased 9% to $5.63 billion, above Wall Street expectations. The company’s wholesale business grew 20%.

As the calendar turns, the heavy lifting of Hill’s corporate overhaul is now complete, just in time for a critical year for Nike and other sportswear brands because of the spotlight created by the Winter Olympics and soccer’s World Cup.

On the call with analysts, Hill reminded participants that Nike has three brands, four sales geographies and does business in 190 countries.

Each is on “different timelines” for recovery, Hill said, before adding, “We’re confident in our path forward.”

title: Columbia Sportswear dares Flat Earthers to literally claim everything
content:
Columbia Sportswear is making one of its boldest marketing statements in recent years with Expedition Impossible, a campaign that blends sharp humor with a clear brand point of view.

The concept is simple and provocative.

Flat Earth believers are invited to photograph the literal edge of the world, with the promise that anyone who succeeds will receive everything owned by the company, Flat Earth, LLC, whose assets are valued at approximately $100,000.

The reward is deliberately expansive. It includes outdoor apparel, performance gear, and a wide range of office assets associated with the company.

Mannequins, snowshoes, toboggans, coffee machines, computers, office plants, and other equipment are all part of the prize, reinforcing the campaign’s exaggerated yet transparent premise.

The full scope of the challenge is revealed through a series of social videos featuring Columbia CEO Tim Boyle.

In the videos, Boyle calmly explains that the winner will receive everything the company owns, while a lawyer intermittently steps in to clarify the legal realities of such a transfer. As Boyle continues to point out item after item, employees look on with visible confusion, steadily building both the value of the prize and the campaign’s understated humor.

The videos are supported by an open letter written by Boyle, formally challenging flat Earth supporters to put their beliefs to the test. The rules are clear. The edge of the Earth must be literal and directly visible, not symbolic or creatively interpreted.

There is one requirement for participation. Anyone attempting the expedition must wear Columbia gear.

That condition reinforces the campaign’s core message. While Expedition Impossible uses humor to spark conversation, its foundation lies in product performance, highlighting Columbia’s reputation for durability, warmth and waterproof protection in extreme conditions.

Expedition Impossible builds on the brand’s “Engineered for Whatever” platform and follows Columbia’s first major brand repositioning in more than a decade. It reflects a shift toward bolder, culturally responsive marketing that embraces conversation instead of avoiding it.

Whether or not the prize is ever claimed is ultimately secondary. By publicly offering all assets owned by Flat Earth, LLC, valued at approximately $100,000, Columbia has already achieved its objective. The campaign has generated attention, fueled discussion, and reinforced a brand posture confident enough to stand at the edge of convention.

title: Lululemon Founder Initiates Proxy Fight to Revamp Board Structure
content:
Lululemon Athletica’s founder, Chip Wilson, has initiated a proxy fight to reform the company’s board structure. This strategic move follows the recent announcement of CEO Calvin McDonald’s departure. Wilson aims to enhance governance at Lululemon, amidst challenges from emerging competitors and pressure from activist investors.

Proxy Fight Launched by Chip Wilson

Chip Wilson formally nominated three independent directors to join Lululemon’s board. The nominations include:

Marc Maurer – Former co-CEO of On Running

Laura Gentile – Former Chief Marketing Officer at ESPN

Eric Hirshberg – Former CEO of Activision

Wilson has expressed concerns regarding board oversight and the lack of a clear succession plan. He stated that the recent CEO change marked a significant failure in leadership, citing a loss of shareholder confidence in the board’s ability to select an effective successor without increased product experience representation.

Context of the Proxy Fight

This proxy fight comes at a critical time for Lululemon. The company has faced difficulties attracting younger and affluent consumers due to rising competition from brands such as Alo Yoga and Vuori. Furthermore, activist investor Elliott Management has been increasing pressure for corporate reform.

Earlier this month, Lululemon confirmed that McDonald would step down in January. His departure adds to the ongoing leadership transitions in the retail sector, reflecting broader instability among global consumer brands.

Currently, Lululemon has not commented publicly on the proxy fight or the situation surrounding its board structure.

title: Lululemon Comments on Chip Wilson Notice to Nominate Director Candidates
content:
lululemon athletica inc. (NASDAQ:LULU) (“lululemon” or the “company”) today commented on Chip Wilson’s announcement that he has submitted a notice to nominate three director candidates to stand for election to the company’s Board at lululemon’s 2026 Annual Meeting of Shareholders:

The lululemon Board of Directors and leadership team have engaged extensively and in good faith for many years with Mr. Wilson to understand his perspectives and communicate our strategy. In our most recent discussions, Mr. Wilson indicated his intent to nominate directors. In the interest of avoiding a costly and distracting proxy fight, the Board requested from Mr. Wilson the names of his director nominees to evaluate their qualifications and backgrounds, but Mr. Wilson declined to engage further. Now that the names have been submitted, the Board will evaluate Mr. Wilson’s director nominees in due course in accordance with the Board’s governance process.

lululemon has a highly engaged and experienced Board that is well-equipped to provide effective guidance on the company’s direction and the execution of our growth strategy. Over one-third of our directors have joined the Board within the past four years.

Our Board and leadership team are focused on driving long-term, sustainable growth, and shareholder value creation. Over the last 10 years, the Board has overseen a significant period of growth, with revenues increasing nearly $9 billion, from $2.1 billion in fiscal year 2015 to $11.0 billion expected in fiscal year 2025 based on our guidance. Over the same time period, income from operations will have grown by nearly 6x. These results have generated significant cash flow that has enabled the company to make substantial investments in the business for growth and to return capital to shareholders through cumulative share repurchases in excess of $5.5 billion since fiscal 2015.

We are encouraged by the strength we are seeing internationally and the work underway in the U.S., but we recognize that further opportunities exist to realize greater value across the company. To help achieve this goal, the Board has initiated a comprehensive search for the company’s next CEO. The Board is focused on identifying a leader with a track record of guiding companies through periods of growth and transformation who can build on our strong foundation and bring fresh perspectives to our brand strategy.

Mr. Wilson has not been involved with the company for a decade, and since his departure, lululemon has continued to adapt to the marketplace and lead the industry, building one of the most compelling growth stories in retail.

The lululemon Board of Directors will continue to take actions that we believe are in the best interests of all the company’s shareholders.

lululemon shareholders do not need to take any action at this time. The Board will review and consider Mr. Wilson’s director candidate nominations and present a formal recommendation regarding his nominations in the company’s definitive proxy statement in advance of the company’s 2026 Annual Meeting of Shareholders.

J.P. Morgan is acting as financial advisor to lululemon and Sidley Austin LLP is serving as legal advisor. Joele Frank, Wilkinson Brimmer Katcher is serving as strategic communications advisor to lululemon.
